Arizona Cardinals.longComment: Conner's 2025 season was cut short due to a right foot injury that required surgery, and he was cleared to take part in practices at the start of training camp. However, he didn't end up mixing into team drills at any point in August before being placed on injured reserve. Though the veteran RB has seemingly made progress in his recovery, the Cardinals are unlikely to rush him back into action with Jeremiyah Love, Tyler Allgeier and Bam Knight already on the 53-man roster. Gambardoro suggests that Conner may be viewed as more of an insurance policy, and it's not out of the question he gets moved ahead of the Nov. 10 trade deadline.

Atlanta Falcons.longComment: Daniels was taken to the hospital quickly after being carted off the field in the third quarter. The linebacker appears to have suffered a significant neck injury, but it may not necessarily threaten any area of his life outside of football.

Bowman suffered a hamstring injury in the second half of Sunday's contest and is not expected to return. If Bowman can't get back on the field in Week 6, Dee Alford should fill most of the void the rest of the way.

Deablo exited the first half of Sunday's contest with an arm injury. The injury is severe enough to rule out the linebacker for the remainder of the contest, meaning the Falcons will need to turn to Harold Perkins at inside linebacker against this Bears offense.

Abdullah was already ruled out for Sunday's game against the Ravens, but his hamstring injury is severe enough for him to warrant a stint on injured reserve. He'll be required to miss at least the next four games, so the earliest Abdullah can return is Week 9 against the Bengals on Sunday, Nov. 8.

Baltimore Ravens.longComment: Bateman appears to have aggravated the shoulder injury that bothered him during Week 6 prep. Now that it's confirmed Bateman won't return Sunday, he'll finish the contest with no catches (on one target). Ja'Kobi Lane, Devontez Walker and LaJohntay Wester are the Ravens' available wide receivers behind top option Zay Flowers.

Vorhees will miss his second straight week due to a foot injury. Emery Jones is expected to get the start in place of Vorhees. With Cam Jurgens inactive with a concussion, Olaivavega Ioane will play at center.

Buffalo Bills.longComment: Oliver will miss a second consecutive game due to the knee injury he sustained during the Bills' Week 4 loss to the Patriots. The defensive tackle will once again be replaced by a mixture of Greg Gaines, DeWayne Carter and T.J. Sanders.

After sitting out a Week 5 overtime win at the Rams, Moore managed just one limited practice (Friday) this week, and he donned a red non-contact jersey while doing so. Per Joe Buscaglia of The Athletic, Moore again didn't log much activity during pregame warmups for a second straight week, forecasting another absence was likely. With Moore's status now clarified, Khalil Shakir, Keon Coleman and Joshua Palmer (shoulder) should earn most of the WR reps in the Bills offense in Week 6.

Carolina Panthers.longComment: Incoom sustained a calf injury quickly after taking over for Jaelan Phillips (hamstring) during Sunday's game. The reserve linebacker will not return to the contest, but Phillips already has resumed his role as the primary weakside linebacker.

Freeling drew the doubtful tag for Week 6 due to a knee injury he sustained against the Lions in Week 4. He won't be available for Sunday's game, but Taylor Moton (illness) has been cleared to play and will serve as the Panthers' starting right tackle. Moton's next opportunity to play is Week 7 against the Buccaneers on Sunday, Oct. 25.

Brooks appears to be making incremental progress in his recovery from core muscle surgery, though he wasn't in uniform Thursday and has yet to be cleared for participation in practice drills while he remains on injured reserve. The 2024 second-round pick has suited up for just five of a possible 38 regular-season games in his career and will miss a minimum of two additional games before he's eligible to return, though his absence could linger beyond then. Chuba Hubbard has worked as the clear lead back for the Panthers, with AJ Dillon (ankle) siphoning off less work than Brooks had been prior to getting hurt.
Jackson will miss the remainder of the campaign after undergoing shoulder surgery. He was also nursing a knee injury and will now shift his focus to getting healthy for the 2027 campaign.

Ekwonu was placed on the Panthers' reserve/PUP list prior to the start of the regular season, as he was still recovering from the ruptured patellar tendon he suffered during the Panthers' wild-card loss against the Rams last postseason, and there's no indication at this point that he's nearing a return. With rookie first-rounder Monroe Freeling now dealing with a knee issue, Stone Forsythe could be called upon to start at right tackle for the Panthers in Week 6 after their bye in Week 5.

Chicago Bears.longComment: Jackson suffered a hip injury in the third quarter. The right guard will likely not return to the contest and has been replaced by Luke Newman.

Stevenson was limited in practice all week by a hip injury, which is severe enough for the fourth-year defensive back to be sidelined for Sunday's contest. The good news for the Bears is that Kyler Gordon (calf) has been cleared to make his 2026 debut, but in Stevenson's absence, Malik Muhammad should continue to operate in an elevated role in the Bears' secondary. Stevenson's next chance to play is Thursday against the Patriots.

Odeyingbo had already been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Falcons, and he'll now be required to miss at least the next four contests. The 27-year-old is second on the team with 3.0 sacks this season. His placement on injured reserve coupled with Montez Sweat's PED suspension is a big hit to the Bears' pass rush.

Cincinnati Bengals.longComment: Hudson will presumably need surgery to address the pec tear and is likely to be placed on injured reserve in the coming days. Though he didn't win a spot on the Bengals' initial 53-man roster coming out of the preseason, Hudson was elevated from the practice squad for two of the team's firs three games before getting signed to the roster Sept. 29. Over his four appearances with Cincinnati, the reserve tight end tallied seven catches for 33 yards and a touchdown on seven targets.

The third-year linebacker out of Southern Miss sustained the injury during Sunday's 31-24 win over the Dolphins, and he'll now be sidelined for at least four weeks after landing on IR. Bozeman had suited up in four of the Bengals' first five contests of the season, seeing most of his action on special teams while tallying four tackles.

Cleveland Browns.longComment: Jefferson exited Sunday's contest in the third quarter with a hip injury. The linebacker's absence means Winston Reid is now the sole depth option behind Quincy Williams and Easton Mascarenas-Arnold for the Browns' defense.
Delpit has entered the NFL's five-step concussion protocol and will not return to Sunday's game. Emmanuel McNeil-Warren will likely finish out the game as the strong safety for the Browns' secondary.
Graham was not expected to suit up for Sunday's game, as he remains limited with knee and ankle injuries. The defensive tackle will again be replaced by Adin Huntington as he continues to recover.

Coming out of the Browns' Week 5 loss to the Jets, head coach Todd Monken labeled Judkins as day-to-day due to a right ankle injury. Judkins was held out of practices Wednesday and Thursday before returning to the field Friday as a limited participant, prompting the Browns to list him questionable heading into the weekend. After going through a pregame workout Sunday, Judkins wasn't able to show enough progress with his ankle to suit up, so he'll wind up being sidelined for the first time this season. The Browns will have Jaleel McLaughlin and Audric Estime as their available running backs for Week 6.

Davis was held out of practice all week, which isn't a great sign given that he was designated to return from injured reserve Oct. 6. If he's not activated from IR by the end of his 21-day window, then Davis would be required to miss the rest of the season. His next chance to play is Week 7 against the Titans on Sunday, Oct. 25.

Sampson has been sidelined since injuring his left knee during a Week 1 loss to the Jaguars, and while he was designated to return from injured reserve Wednesday, he didn't do enough in practice since then to warrant activation. With Sampson still sidelined and Quinshon Judkins' (foot) status up in the air for Week 6, the Browns may be looking at a situation in which Jaleel McLaughlin and Audric Estime are powering the ground game this weekend.

Sanders opened the year as Cleveland's No. 3 running back but saw his role increase after Dylan Sampson (knee) landed on IR. During the season's first four games, Sanders gained 42 yards on eight carries and added eight catches for 49 yards on nine targets before going down with a hip injury in Week 5. Sanders will be sidelined for at least the next four games.

Dallas Cowboys.longComment: Porter sat out a Thursday night loss to the Buccaneers in Week 5 due to an illness, and after sandwiching two limited sessions around a full practice Thursday while he managed an ankle injury, he took a questionable tag into Sunday. Assuming he's active for the Week 6 contest, Porter will line up as one of the Cowboys' starting outside cornerbacks along with DaRon Bland.

Overshown has been sidelined since going down in Week 1 against the Giants and will miss a fifth consecutive game. Jaishawn Barham and Dee Winters will continue to handle linebacker duties for the Cowboys.
The fourth-round rookie offensive lineman has logged just five offensive snaps and another 17 on special teams through four appearances this season.

Durant will end up missing a fourth consecutive game due to a hamstring injury that he picked up against the Commanders in Week 2. If Joey Porter (ankle) is also unable to play, then Ameer Speed (knee) would be the next man up at outside cornerback opposite DaRon Bland. Durant's next chance to play is Week 7 against the Eagles on Monday, Oct. 26.

Denver Broncos.longComment: Badie suffered a thumb injury in the first half and was considered questionable to return. Now that he has been ruled out for the remainder of Thursday's contest, RJ Harvey and J.K. Dobbins should each get a few more touches.

Surtain was held out of practice all week by an ankle injury, which will cause him to miss a second consecutive game. Meanwhile, fellow starting outside cornerback Riley Moss (ribs) earned the questionable tag for Thursday's game, and, if he returns, the second starting spot would go to one of Jahdae Barron or Kris Abrams-Draine. Surtain's next opportunity to play is Week 7 against the Cardinals on Sunday, Oct. 25.

Because of his placement on IR due to an ankle injury, Bryant will be required to miss at least the next four games. The earliest he can return is Week 9 against the Panthers on Sunday, Nov. 11, but with the Broncos on bye for Week 10, the second-year wide receiver could be held out until Week 11 against the Raiders in late November. Troy Franklin figures to step into the WR3 role behind Courtland Sutton and Jaylen Waddle for as long as Bryant is sidelined.

Detroit Lions.longComment: Bartch has already missed three games due to a foot injury that he sustained against the Bills in Week 2. While on IR, he'll be forced to miss at least four games, so Week 11 against the Buccaneers on Sunday, Nov. 22, is the earliest he can return.

White was diagnosed with a broken forearm following the Lions' Week 5 win over the Cardinals. He'll be required to miss at least the next four games on IR, and while he's likely to be sidelined past that minimum window, there's optimism that the veteran linebacker will return at some point this season. Malcolm Rodriguez is the next man up at linebacker in White's absence.

Kennedy suffered a season-ending MCL injury in his right knee during the Lions' Week 5 win over the Cardinals. His move to IR opens a spot on Detroit's 53-man roster, and in his absence, Jacob Saylors is in line to take over return duties on kickoffs and punts.

Mays' 21-day window to return from injured reserve opened Wednesday, and he was a limited practice participant all week. He's not quite ready to return, but with the Lions on a bye for Week 6, Mays' next chance to play is Week 7 against Green Bay on Sunday, Oct. 25.

Branch returned to practice Wednesday after the Lions opened up his 21-day practice window. The strong safety managed to log limited practice in all three Week 5 prep sessions but is not quite ready to return to the field. Christian Izien will continue to start at strong safety while Branch puts the finishing touches on his recovery.

Green Bay Packers.longComment: Ford emerged from this past Sunday's win over Chicago with a calf injury and didn't practice at all this week. He's now slated to miss a minimum of four contests while on IR. Ford has been working in a rotational role along Green Bay's defensive line this season and has amassed five tackles, including 0.5 sacks, through five contests.

Hargrave suffered a season-ending torn Achilles in last Sunday's win over the Bears, so this move is a mere formality. Green Bay's defense continues to be hit by injuries, as the unit awaits Micah Parsons' (knee) season debut. Chris McClellan and Anthony Campbell (ankle) will be next up for heavier snap loads up front on the defensive line.

Williams remains questionable for Sunday night against the Cowboys, but the transaction Saturday paves the way for him to play versus Dallas. With Skyy Moore (ankle) joining Jayden Reed (neck) on injured reserve Saturday, Williams could see offensive snaps behind Christian Watson and Matthew Golden, and there's a real chance Williams takes over WR3 duties in Green Bay moving forward. Bo Melton and J. Michael Sturdivant are his main competitors for snaps on offense.

Moore wasn't able to return after injuring his ankle last Sunday against the Bears, and in the midst of not practicing during Week 6 prep, he was seen wearing a boot on his left boot and using a scooter to move about the locker room, per Matt Schneidman of The Athletic. Moore thus will miss at least the next four games, meaning his next chance to suit up will be Sunday, Nov. 15 against the Vikings. In Moore's absence, some combination of Bo Melton, Savion Williams (ankle) and Matthew Golden likely will handle return duties.
Monk was limited in practice all week due to a lingering quad injury that held him out for the Packers' last two games. His return would bolster Green Bay's interior offensive line.
Banks was limited in practice all week by knee and toe injuries. Laken Tomlinson would likely start at left guard if Banks is ruled out for a fourth consecutive game.

St-Juste was unable to practice all week due to a hamstring injury, which he aggravated during the Packers' Week 5 win over the Bears. His next chance to play is Week 7 against the Lions on Sunday, Oct. 25.

Cisse popped up on Friday's injury report as a limited participant due to a hip injury. His status could change over the weekend, but whether he'll play Sunday may not be officially known until the Packers announce their list of inactive players approximately 90 minutes before the 8:20 p.m. ET kickoff. Carrington Valentine would likely start opposite Keisean Nixon at outside cornerback if Cisse is not cleared to play.

Jacobs' playing status has been in limbo since his May arrest following a domestic incident that led to the running back pleading no contest to misdemeanor charges of battery and criminal damage to property in early September. He since has missed the first five games of the season and will miss a sixth contest Sunday, and while he'll be able to practice next week and make his 2026 debut on Sunday, Oct. 25, the NFL will keep its investigation of Jacobs open, reserving the right to add further discipline if new information comes to light, per Adam Schefter of ESPN.

Riley has been on the active/PUP list since Aug. 31 while continuing to recover from a torn Achilles tendon. The defensive lineman made his return to practice Wednesday, logging a limited session to open the week. With Javon Hargrave (Achilles) done for the season, Riley's return to action will be a welcomed one, whenever that may be.

Parsons had previously noted in the early stages of training camp that the Week 6 matchup with his former team was a realistic target for his season debut. The 27-year-old ultimately won't be ready to play against Dallas, and while the Packers remain hopeful he'll be able to return to action at some point in October, his absence looks increasingly likely to stretch into November since he has yet to resume practicing with the team. Green Bay hasn't indicated that Parsons has experienced any setbacks from the torn ACL in his left knee that he sustained Dec. 14, as the team may simply be taking a deliberate approach with the star pass rusher's recovery.

Houston Texans.longComment: Blankenship was deemed to have a concussion by one of the NFL's independent neurologists. The safety has now entered the league's five-step concussion protocol and will not participate in full-contact practices or games until he is cleared. M.J. Stewart will likely finish the game at strong safety alongside Calen Bullock.

Currently in the midst of his second week of practicing with the Texans after having his 21-day evaluation window opened Oct. 7, Dell has taken a notable step forward in his recovery from a severe left knee injury by turning in back-to-back full sessions Wednesday and Thursday. Though the Texans won't bring him back from injured reserve for the London game, Dell stands a strong chance of being activated ahead of the team's Oct. 25 matchup with the Giants and seeing his first game action since December 2024 if he can continue to practice without restrictions next week.

Indianapolis Colts.longComment: Sanchez injured his foot in the fourth quarter when the Titans blocked his punt for a touchdown. With Sanchez questionable to return, kicker Spencer Shrader may have to take over punting duties for the Colts' special teams.

Gardner exited the third quarter of Sunday's game with a calf injury. The cornerback returned to the locker room with what appears to be a significant issue. Cam Taylor-Britt is in at outside cornerback opposite Charvarius Ward.

Gould suffered a concussion in the second half and has since been ruled out for the rest of Sunday's meeting with the Titans. With Ashton Dulin (ankle) sidelined, Gould had been seeing some action on special teams. However, Seth McGowan and Josh Downs will need to be more involved in that area the rest of the way.

Warren was labeled as a game-time decision for Sunday's AFC South tilt after the second-year tight end popped up on Friday's injury report due to a lingering groin injury from training camp. Warren has seen at least seven targets in three of his last four games, and those opportunities will be absorbed by tight ends Mo Alie-Cox and Will Mallory, as well as wide receivers Josh Downs and Keenan Allen.

It's a sign that Pierce is progressing in his recovery from a left heel injury that he aggravated during the Colts' Week 2 overtime loss to the Chiefs. The earliest he is eligible to return from injured reserve is Week 7 against the Vikings, and while Pierce opted for rehab and avoided surgery, Boyd believes that the fifth-year wide receiver is not close to a return. Josh Downs popped up on Wednesday's injury report with a hamstring injury, so Keenan Allen could be the Colts' top wide receiver for Sunday's AFC South showdown against the Titans.

Key sustained a hamstring injury against the Colts in Week 4, and the injury is severe enough for the veteran defensive lineman to warrant a stint on IR. He'll be required to miss at least four games, so the earliest Key can return is Week 9 against the Cowboys on Sunday, Nov. 8. Laiatu Latu, Jaylahn Tuimoloau and rookie fifth-rounder George Gumbs are all in line for more defensive snaps in Key's absence.

Jacksonville Jaguars.longComment: The Jaguars had listed Johnson as questionable to return after he left in the second quarter due to the ankle injury, but though he was spotted on the sideline in the second half, he never checked back into the contest. Kaevon Merriweather ended up serving as the primary replacement at safety for Johnson, who will have a Week 7 bye to recover from his injury before potentially returning to action Nov. 1 versus the Colts. Johnson accrued six tackles prior to his departure.

The Jaguars have yet to confirm the report, but the left tackle can be safely ruled out for Sunday's game against the Texans in London and could be at risk of missing additional time following the team's Week 7 bye. After Harrison was unable to check back into this past Sunday's win over the Eagles, Walker Little stepped in as his replacement at left tackle. Little could be headed for a start in Week 6 if the Jaguars opt to keep starting right tackle Cole Van Lanen at his current position.

Kansas City Chiefs.longComment: The transaction frees up a spot on the 53-man roster for linebacker Cam Jones, who was signed off the practice squad. After dislocating his left ankle in the Chiefs' Oct. 4 win over the Raiders and requiring surgery, Thornton is facing an estimated recovery timeline of 3-to-4 months, which means that he'll likely be sidelined until at least Week 17 or 18 in a best-case scenario. While Thornton is out, the Chiefs are expected to lean on Jalen Royals and Cyrus Allen to handle more reps in three-receiver sets alongside starters Rashee Rice (hamstring) and Xavier Worthy.

Las Vegas Raiders.longComment: Runyon opened the season on injured reserve due to a lower-body injury. His 21-day practice window opened Wednesday, and he was a limited practice participant in all three sessions during Week 6 prep. That's not quite enough for Runyon to make his 2026 debut, but his next opportunity to do so is Week 7 against the Rams on Sunday, Oct. 25.

Thornton has been a full practice participant for two weeks, and he can practice for one more week before the Raiders have to make a decision on activating him from IR or leaving him there for the rest of the year. He'll likely be activated, but it isn't clear there's a role for him in the offense.

Los Angeles Chargers.longComment: McConkey was being evaluated for a possible head injury early in the second quarter before the Chargers quickly ruled him out. This follows a nearly three-week stretch in which he was dealing with a lingering foot issue that didn't allow him to log a snap in Week 4, despite being active. Now that he's subject to the concussion protocol, McConkey's next game action is up in the air.

Shelly didn't play in Week 5 against the Broncos. He was listed as doubtful heading into the meeting with Kansas City but will now miss his second consecutive contest. With Donte Jackson (hamstring) also sidelined, Deane Leonard is the favorite to start opposite Cam Hart at corner.

Dupree suffered a neck injury in the Week 5 meeting with the Broncos. He practiced in a limited capacity a few times during the week but ended up receiving a questionable tag. Now that Dupree has been ruled out, rookie Akheem Mesidor is in line for more snaps.

Alt will be sidelined for a second straight game, but assuming his neck responds well while he begins ramping back up, he could be back in the lineup for the Chargers' next contest Week 8 versus the Rams on Nov. 1. Alex Harkey replaced Alt at right tackle in the Week 5 loss to the Broncos and could draw another start in his stead Sunday.

Per Noah Furtado of The Athletic, Ingold wasn't included on the Chargers' initial Week 6 injury report Wednesday before being a late addition on account of the shoulder issue. He'll be sidelined for at least the next four games, making him ineligible to play until Week 11 versus the Jets on Nov. 22. The fullback hadn't logged any carries and recorded three receptions for 35 yards on four targets through Los Angeles' first five games.

Per Ricardo Sandoval of USA Today, Harbaugh said back on Sept. 1 that he expected Perryman to spend the minimum four games on IR due to his unspecified injury, but the veteran linebacker will now be sidelined for a sixth straight game to begin the campaign. The 33-year-old appeared in 10 games for the Chargers in 2025, logging 47 tackles and three pass breakups.

Los Angeles Rams.longComment: Grupe suffered a knee injury while making a tackle on kickoff-return coverage in the first quarter. The kicker is doubtful to return, leaving Punter Ethan Evans to operate as the team's placekicker for the remainder of the game.

McDuffie sat out Friday's practice with a groin injury after getting hurt in Thursday's session. The precautionary absence appears to have revealed a real injury, and now Emmanuel Forbes will be starting opposite Jaylen Watson at outside cornerback for the Rams' Sunday divisional matchup with the Cardinals.

Garrett underwent knee surgery following the Rams' Week 1 loss to the 49ers in Australia and was subsequently placed on injured reserve. He's eligible to return from IR now that he's missed the four-game minimum, but Garrett has not progressed enough in his recovery to practice, even in a limited capacity. A six-week recovery timeline for the superstar pass rusher's return was reported by Ian Rapoport of NFL Network and ESPN in late September, and if that timeline is accurate, then Garrett could be back in action for Week 7 against the Raiders on Sunday, Oct. 25.

Miami Dolphins.longComment: Brents had initially been labeled as questionable to return after leaving the game in the first half to receive evaluation for a concussion as well as the stinger. He was able to check back into the game to begin the second half, but he appears to have suffered an aggravation of the stinger. Brents tallied six tackles and one pass breakup prior to his most recent exit.

Taaffe exited the third quarter of Sunday's contest with a chest injury. The reserve strong safety's absence means that Julius Wood will have to fill in at strong safety if Dante Trader must leave the contest.
The 2025 second-round pick exited in the second quarter of the contest. If Savaiinaea is unable to return, Jarrett Kingston will likely serve as his replacement at right guard.
Duck remains on the reserve/PUP list. After practicing in full this week, Duck will have a better chance to suit up in Week 7 following Miami's bye next week.

Minnesota Vikings.longComment: Mason has already missed the required four games after landing on injured reserve following the Vikings' season-opening win over the Packers, and he'll get additional time to recover from thumb surgery while the team is on bye Week 6. Assuming that Mason's thumb has healed as expected following the five-week absence, he'll likely be designated for return from IR and resume practicing coming out of the bye. Aaron Jones has shouldered the load out of the Minnesota backfield over the past four games, but Mason should reclaim the bulk of the snaps on early downs once he's reinstated from IR.

After recording a seven-yard reception on the Vikings' opening possession, Hockenson immediately headed to the locker room to get checked for a head injury. With Minnesota confirming that he has sustained a concussion, Hockenson will be shut down for the rest of the afternoon and will now be subject to the NFL's five-step protocol. Minnesota is on bye in Week 6, so Hockenson's next chance to play will come against the Colts on Oct. 25.

Jackson suffered a torn meniscus during Sunday's 15-10 win over Miami, and he was already set to miss the rest of the regular season, so Tuesday's move to the IR comes as no surprise. Joe Huber is the top candidate to take over as Minnesota's starting left guard in Jackson's absence.

Oliver's move to IR was expected after the tight end was diagnosed with a torn bicep Monday. The tight end will likely miss most, if not all, of the 2026 season as he recovers from surgery. T.J. Hockenson and Gavin Bartholomew are now the only tight ends on the Vikings' roster, meaning practice-squad elevations ahead of Week 4 will likely include at least one more option at the position. The Vikings signed linebacker Kyle Van Noy to the 53-man roster in a corresponding move.

New England Patriots.longComment: After suffering an ankle injury in Sunday's meeting with the Jets, Moses didn't return. With the short turnaround for the Patriots ahead of Thursday's game against the Bears, the 35-year-old may not have time to recover and play. For now, Moses should at least be considered questionable, but if he can't suit up, Caleb Lomu may operate in his place.
Brown suffered a knee injury in the fourth quarter and has since been downgraded to out. Walter Rouse entered the contest and will presumably fill the void for the remainder of the game.

Vera-Tucker sustained a hamstring injury in the second quarter of Sunday's contest. The left guard's absence has shifted the Patriots' offensive line around, leaving Ben Brown at left guard and Matt Pryor at right guard.

Doubs was injured on his 42-yard TD catch in the first quarter, after which he went to the sideline tent, and eventually, the locker room. A shoulder issue was the cause for his exit and will keep him out for the rest of Week 6. A.J. Brown, DeMario Douglas, Efton Chism and Kyle Williams are the Patriots' remaining healthy and available wide receivers.

Canada will miss a third consecutive week due to a hamstring injury he suffered during Week 4 prep. The reserve option for the Patriots' secondary has an unclear return timeline but should have more grace due to the return of starting option Christian Gonzalez.

Bryant suffered an ankle injury in the preseason. The offensive tackle has served his regular-season, four-game minimum on IR and is ready to return to the field. Bryant was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice, and the Patriots have until Nov. 4 to return him to the active roster, or he will finish the 2026 season on IR.

New Orleans Saints.longComment: McKinstry exited Sunday's contest after experiencing a sudden onset of a migraine. Until there is a more definitive update, he should at least be considered questionable for the Week 7 meeting with the Steelers in Paris. If McKinstry can't suit up for that one, Quincy Riley is a candidate for more snaps.

Riley suffered a neck injury late in the fourth quarter of Sunday's contest. Coach Kellen Moore seemed confident that the cornerback was okay, but Week 7 preparation should more accurately reflect Riley's current state.

After suffering a knee injury in the first half of Sunday's meeting with New York, Ruiz was listed as questionable to return. However, Ruiz has since been ruled out, meaning Jeremiah Wright will continue to see more snaps the rest of the way.

Shepherd will be sidelined for a second consecutive game due to an illness, which prevented him from participating in any practice during Week 6 prep. Rookie second-rounder Christen Miller should see a bump in defensive snaps due to the absence of Shepherd, whose next opportunity to play is Week 7 against the Steelers on Sunday, Oct. 25.

Tyson has resided on injured reserve all season after sustaining a right hamstring strain during an Aug. 13 training camp practice. Though the rookie first-round pick hasn't hit any reported snags in his recovery, the Saints aren't yet ready to open his 21-day practice window. Adam Schefter of ESPN previously reported that Tyson wouldn't make his NFL debut until Week 7, but because the young wideout hasn't resumed practicing yet, a return to game action following the Saints' Week 8 bye is probably more realistic at this point.

New York Giants.longComment: Mooney sustained a neck injury in the second half of Sunday's game. The wide receiver will need to be thoroughly vetted for a significant injury before potentially being allowed to return to the contest. Charlie Jones will operate as the Giants' No. 3 wide receiver while Mooney is absent.

Newsome exited Sunday's game with a head injury. The cornerback was diagnosed with a concussion and has now entered the NFL's five-step concussion protocol. Newsome will need to be cleared by an independent neurologist to return to full-contact football activities.

Berrios suffered a foot injury in the Week 5 victory over the Cardinals. He has since been ruled out for the remainder of the 2026 season and is currently occupying a spot on injured reserve. It's unknown if Berrios will be cleared to suit up for the start of the 2027 campaign, but while he is sidelined this season, Charlie Jones is projected to handle most of the return duties.

New York Jets.longComment: Mauigoa left in the first half of Sunday's game with a thigh injury. The 23-year-old will be further evaluated by medical staff to determine if he can return. Trevin Wallace may see more time in a depth role should Mauigoa remain out.

Philadelphia Eagles.longComment: Smith took a hit from Chuba Hubbard in the second quarter. He exited for an evaluation in the medical tent and was then escorted to the locker room by the training staff. With Smith ruled out for the remainder of Week 6, the Eagles will need to rely on Jonathan Greenard, Arnold Ebiketie and Keyshawn James-Newby to fill the void.

Steele exited the first quarter, recording no carries and one four-yard reception before his departure. If Steele is unable to return, Jaydon Blue will be left as the only reserve option behind starting running back Dameon Pierce.

The decision comes as no surprise, given that Epenesa was listed as doubtful for Sunday's contest. He'll miss his first game of the season due to a back injury, and his next opportunity to play is Week 7 against the Cowboys on Monday, Oct. 26.

Bennett hasn't yet played this season after hurting his knee during training camp. However, he had his 21-day practice window opened Wednesday and upgraded to full practice participation Friday following a pair of limited sessions, so the third-year cornerback could make his season debut next Monday against Dallas.

Dickerson remains on injured reserve after he wasn't activated Saturday despite having his 21-day practice window opened earlier in the week. Willie Lampkin should make another start at left guard for the Eagles.

Stowers will have to wait at least another week before making his regular-season NFL debut after he had his 21-day practice window opened earlier this week. Stowers should see snaps as a catch-first tight end behind Dallas Goedert once he's ready to return to game action.

Calcaterra remains on injured reserve, though his 21-day practice window was opened earlier in the week. He's nearing a return, though his role is unclear behind Dallas Goedert and potentially even block-first TE Johnny Mundt.

After prior reports indicated that a stint on injured reserve wouldn't be necessary, Hurts will now go on IR after multiple consultations with doctors for the superficial blood clot in his calf. As a result of the transaction, Hurts will be required to miss at least four games, though the quarterback is out indefinitely and isn't a lock to be activated Week 11 when first eligible. Tanner McKee will step in as the Eagles' starting quarterback beginning with Sunday's game against the Panthers, while rookie fifth-round pick Cole Payton will elevate into the backup role.

Pittsburgh Steelers.longComment: Echols was injured on a Buccaneers punt in the first half. He limped off the field and was eventually ruled out coming out of halftime due to a hamstring injury. With Echols done for the remainder of Week 6, rookie Daylen Everette will need to step up.

Wilson already had been ruled out for Sunday's game against Tampa Bay, but the move to IR means that the third-year pro will be required to miss at least four games. Since the Steelers are on a bye for Week 9, the earliest that Wilson can return is Week 11 against the Eagles on Sunday, Nov. 22. He joins Michael Pittman (foot) on injured reserve, which leaves rookie second-rounder Germie Bernard as the Steelers' WR2 behind DK Metcalf for the next few weeks.

Elliott's 21-day return window was opened Oct. 8. The safety did not play in the Steelers' Week 5 game against the Colts and has now been ruled out ahead of Week 6. Elliott was a limited participant in all three practices during Week 6 prep but is still not quite ready to return to the field.

With the expected move now official, Pittman will be required to miss at least the next four games, making Week 10 against the Bengals on Sunday, Nov. 15 the earliest that the veteran wide receiver can return. Roman Wilson and Germie Bernard are both in line for more offensive snaps for as long as Pittman is sidelined.

San Francisco 49ers.longComment: Williams made his season debut last Sunday against the Seahawks, recording a pair of tackles (one solo) on 36.5 percent of the defensive snaps. Working his way back to full strength off last season's torn ACL, Williams' role should continue to slowly grow over the next several weeks.

Stout was limited in practice all week after he initially injured the shoulder in Week 4 against the Broncos. He's yet to miss a game this season. Across five appearances, the cornerback has 16 tackles (nine solo), including 0.5 sacks, and one pass breakup.

Sigle is dealing with a high-ankle sprain that he suffered Week 4 versus Denver. The second-year safety missed this past Sunday's win over Seattle and is now set to sit out a second straight game. In Sigle's absence, Malik Mustapha will likely draw another start.

Though the decision was made not to put Bosa on IR, he's now set to miss his fourth straight game. Head coach Kyle Shanahan said early this week that the veteran edge rusher had a chance to play against Washington, but Bosa didn't end up practicing at all. While it's not out of the question that he could return Week 7 in Atlanta, it wouldn't be surprising if San Francisco opts to hold Bosa out for that contest as well given that the 49ers have a bye Week 8.

The 49ers officially listed Kirk as questionable for Week 6 after opening his practice window this week, which allowed him to log limited practices Thursday and Friday. Shanahan hinted Saturday that Kirk has a chance to make his 49ers debut Monday, and a call on that front could be contingent on the health of top wide receiver Mike Evans (ribs/Achilles). With Deebo Samuel (hamstring) sidelined for the foreseeable future and three other WRs on IR, Brandin Cooks, Jacob Cowing and Jordan Watkins are the only healthy options at the position on the active roster.

Evans worked to the side during each of the 49ers' last two practices while nursing injuries to his ribs and Achilles. That was enough for him to draw the questionable tag for MNF, and there's also a chance that Christian Kirk (calf) will be activated from injured reserve before the game, per Nick Wagoner of ESPN.com. Deebo Samuel (hamstring) has already been ruled out, so Brandin Cooks, Jacob Cowing, Jordan Watkins and tight end George Kittle would all carry heaver workloads in the passing game if Evans joins Samuel on the sidelines for Week 6.

It was reported earlier in the week that Samuel would miss multiple weeks; however, the 49ers are stopping short of placing him on injured reserve for the time being due to how the schedule sets up. Samuel is set to miss at least the Week 6 game against the Commanders and likely the following game against the Falcons before the team gets a bye. Week 9 seems to be the earliest potential return date for the veteran.

Robinson is on the mend from a right high-ankle sprain, which he sustained in the 49ers' Week 2 win over the Dolphins. The 49ers have a dire need for reinforcements at receiver with Deebo Samuel (hamstring) out through the bye and three other wideouts currently on IR, but unless he has his 21-day window opened next week and looks better than expected in practice, Robinson doesn't look like he'll be able to help the team until its Week 9 game versus the Raiders.

Martin opened the regular season on injured reserve due to a hamstring injury that he sustained during training camp in August. Shanahan said Martin is "getting close" to returning to practice, and if he's cleared for field work this week, his participation level will shed light on whether he'll play in Week 6 against the Commanders on Monday, Oct. 19. The 2025 third-rounder logged 11 tackles (eight solo) and one fumble recovery across seven regular-season games during his rookie campaign, which he finished on injured reserve due to a concussion.

Shanahan seemingly ruled out the reserve linebacker through the 49ers' Week 8 bye, with Wallow expected to sit out Week 6 versus the Commanders as well as Week 7 in Atlanta. Wallow has accrued seven tackles (five solo) this season while seeing the majority of his playing time on special teams.

Seattle Seahawks.longComment: Price was placed on injured reserve after Week 3 due to a lingering chest injury, and while he must miss one more contest to meet the minimum four-game requirement on the list, he appears as if he'll be ready to go when first eligible in Week 8 against the Bears on Monday, Nov. 2. In the meantime, the Seahawks are expected to get back fellow RB Zach Charbonnet (knee), so Price may be relegated to a lessened role once he's healthy enough to play again.

Surratt was unable to practice at all this week and he will now be forced to miss a third straight contest while nursing a calf injury. In Surratt's absence, Seattle will once again have to find a fill-in for his workload with the special-teams unit.

Following the first two walkthroughs of Week 6 prep, Thomas was unable to practice in any capacity Wednesday and will miss his first game of the season due to an ankle injury. It's not exactly clear who will start alongside Ernest Jones at inside linebacker in Thomas' absence, but Tyrice Knight and Patrick O'Connell figure to be the top candidates to do so. Thomas' next opportunity to play is Week 7 against the Chiefs on Sunday, Oct. 25.

The Seahawks opened Charbonnet's practice window to return from the reserve/PUP list on Oct. 1, but he's yet to log anything more than a limited practice since then. The team now has until next Thursday, Oct. 22, to activate him, or else he'll be required to miss the rest of the season by rule. Of course, Seattle does expect Charbonnet to play this season, so even if he isn't ready to play in Week 7, the move will be made next week. In the meantime, Emanuel Wilson will continue to lead the backfield, with George Holani backing him up.

Tampa Bay Buccaneers.longComment: Tucker ended Week 6 prep with consecutive limited sessions as he manages a quadriceps injury. The running back is not quite ready to return to the field and will not suit up for Sunday's game. Josh Williams has been elevated from the practice squad to serve as the Buccaneers' No. 3 running back behind Bucky Irving and Kenny Gainwell on Sunday.

Morrison enterted the weekend doubtful to suit up for Sunday's game. The cornerback was limited throughout Week 6 prep with a quadriceps injury and will not be able to overcome the injury in time for Sunday's game. Kevin Knowles will likely start at outside cornerback against the Steelers.

Sills' 21-day practice window opened Monday, but the wide receiver remains on injured reserve. The 30-year-old logged three consecutive full practices during Week 6 prep and should be set to suit up as long as the Buccaneers are comfortable utilizing a roster spot. If the team decides to hold Sills on IR, he will need to wait until at least Week 7 to make his 2026 debut.

Tennessee Titans.longComment: Adams exited in the first half of Sunday's game with an ankle injury. The 27-year-old has five tackles (two solo) and one pass deflection prior to exiting.

Washington Commanders.longComment: Jean-Baptiste didn't practice at all this week, so it's not a surprise that he won't play Monday. Per Reed, head coach Dan Quinn expects rookie Joshua Josephs to see more playing time Week 6, with both Jean-Baptiste and Charles Omenihu (groin/ankle) sidelined.

This will be Omehihu's second straight absence after he was injured early against Indianapolis in Week 4. The Commanders are on bye next week, so the veteran defensive end will look to return in Week 8 against Philadelphia. Javon Kinlaw (ankle/knee) is questionable for Monday's contest, so Washington may need to lean more on Shy Tuttle and/or Deatrich Wise.

McNichols was a full practice participant this week but remains on injured reserve, though the Commanders could still choose to activate him ahead of Monday night's contest. With Jacory Croskey-Merritt (foot) out, the Commanders could use McNichols as depth alongside Rachaad White and Austin Ekeler.

Diggs ended the week with back-to-back limited practices, which was enough for him to draw the questionable tag for Monday Night Football. Diggs did not play in Week 5 against the Giants, but if he's cleared to play against the 49ers, then it would be the first time that he, Terry McLaurin and Jayden Daniels are on the field together since Week 2 against the Cowboys. If Diggs does not play, then Antonio Williams and Treylon Burks would both operate in elevated roles offensively behind McLaurin.

As expected, Mariota will miss a second consecutive game due to a sprained MCL in his right knee, which he picked up during the Commanders' Week 4 loss to the Colts in London. Rookie seventh-rounder Athan Kaliakmanis will once again serve as Washington's backup quarterback behind Jayden Daniels for Monday night's game. The Commanders are on a bye for Week 7, so Mariota could be back in action for Week 8 against the Eagles on Sunday, Nov. 1.

Croskey-Merritt was unable to practice all week due to a groin injury, and he's now been officially ruled out for Monday night's game. The statuses of Rachaad White (shoulder) and Austin Ekeler (chest) will be known once the Commanders announce their injury designations on Saturday's practice report. Washington is on a bye for Week 7, so Croskey-Merritt will have more time to recover from his injury before the Commanders' Week 8 tilt against the Eagles on Sunday, Nov. 1.

Magee suffered a hamstring injury in the Week 1 loss to Philadelphia. As a result, he was placed on injured reserve and missed the last four contests. Magee can be activated any time in the next 21 days, meaning there's a chance he will suit up Monday night against the 49ers.
